interpro/panther/PTHR30607/PTHR30607-rev.preferred_name: KdpA potassium-binding and translocating subunit of KdpFABC
interpro/panther/PTHR30607/PTHR30607-rev.summary: KdpA is the potassium-selective, membrane-embedded subunit of the KdpFABC high-affinity potassium uptake complex found in many bacteria and some archaea. It belongs to the superfamily of K+ transporters (SKT) and carries a channel-like selectivity filter formed by four M1-P-M2 repeats. KdpA binds periplasmic K+ and passes it through an intramembrane tunnel to the membrane domain of the P-type ATPase subunit KdpB, which releases it into the cytoplasm at the expense of ATP. KdpA does not hydrolyse ATP itself: the complete reaction of P-type potassium transport is a property of the assembled KdpFABC complex, to which KdpA contributes substrate selection and translocation.
interpro/panther/PTHR30607/PTHR30607-rev.coherence_reason: PANTHER resolves a single subfamily (SF2) and a single PAINT node for this family. Every reviewed member is annotated as KdpA of a Kdp operon, and the selectivity-filter architecture is shared. There are no known divergent paralog groups; the main interpretive caution is that the transporter activity is a complex-level activity to which KdpA contributes.

interpro/panther/PTHR43743/PTHR43743-rev.preferred_name: KdpB P-type ATPase subunit of KdpFABC
interpro/panther/PTHR43743/PTHR43743-rev.summary: KdpB is the catalytic, pump-like subunit of the KdpFABC high-affinity potassium uptake complex of bacteria and some archaea. It is a type IA member of the P-type ATPase superfamily, with seven transmembrane helices and the phosphorylation (P), nucleotide-binding (N) and actuator (A) cytoplasmic domains. ATP hydrolysis proceeds through a 4-aspartylphosphate intermediate in the P domain; the energy is coupled to release of K+ that the channel-like subunit KdpA delivers through an intramembrane tunnel. In E. coli, phosphorylation of a serine in the KdpB A domain (Ser162) inhibits the complex. KdpB orthologs are confined to Kdp systems, so the family is a reliable marker of KdpFABC.
interpro/panther/PTHR43743/PTHR43743-rev.coherence_reason: PANTHER resolves a single subfamily (SF1) and one PAINT node. All reviewed members are KdpB subunits of Kdp operons; other type IA/IB P-type ATPases sit in separate PANTHER families. The activity is shared by the whole family, but it is a complex-level transport activity to which KdpB contributes ATP hydrolysis and energy coupling.

interpro/panther/PTHR30042/PTHR30042-rev.summary: KdpC is a single-transmembrane-helix subunit of the KdpFABC high-affinity potassium uptake complex, with a large periplasmic domain. It has no known homologues outside Kdp systems and no catalytic activity of its own. In E. coli it is essential for a functional complex and has been described as a catalytic chaperone that raises the ATP affinity of KdpB through a transient KdpB-KdpC-ATP ternary complex; its periplasmic domain has also been proposed to cap the KdpA pore. Its contribution to transport is therefore accessory and complex-dependent.
interpro/panther/PTHR30042/PTHR30042-rev.coherence_reason: A single PANTHER subfamily (SF2) and one PAINT node with a single loss row. All characterized members are KdpC subunits of Kdp operons. The caution for this family is not heterogeneity but the level of the assertion: the transporter activity belongs to the assembled complex, not to KdpC alone.

interpro/panther/PTHR45569/PTHR45569-rev.preferred_name: KdpD sensor histidine kinase of the KdpD/KdpE two-component system
interpro/panther/PTHR45569/PTHR45569-rev.summary: KdpD is the membrane-bound sensor histidine kinase that, with the response regulator KdpE, controls expression of the kdpFABC potassium-uptake operon. Full-length members have a cytoplasmic N-terminal KdpD domain, four transmembrane segments, a cytoplasmic universal-stress-protein (Usp)-like and GAF region, and a C-terminal transmitter region with the phosphoacceptor histidine (His673 in E. coli) and the kinase catalytic domain. In E. coli KdpD autophosphorylates in trans within a homodimer in response to potassium limitation and related signals and transfers the phosphoryl group to KdpE. Some cyanobacterial members are truncated and lack the transmitter region.
interpro/panther/PTHR45569/PTHR45569-rev.coherence_reason: A single PANTHER subfamily (SF1). Most members, including E. coli, Clostridium acetobutylicum, Mycobacterium tuberculosis and Staphylococcus aureus KdpD and P. putida KT2440 KdpD, are full-length sensor kinases. The Synechocystis member P73870 is only 370 residues long, too short to contain the transmitter region that occupies residues 670-883 of E. coli KdpD, so it cannot have the kinase activity inherited from the family root.

interpro/panther/PTHR48111/PTHR48111-rev.summary: A large family of two-component response regulators with an N-terminal receiver domain and a C-terminal winged helix-turn-helix (OmpR/PhoB-type) DNA-binding output domain. Phosphotransfer from a cognate sensor histidine kinase to a conserved receiver aspartate drives dimerization and binding to promoter regions, so that each regulator controls the regulon of its own signalling pathway. Characterized members include E. coli OmpR, PhoB, PhoP, CpxR, ArcA, BaeR, BasR, CreB, TorR and KdpE, Pseudomonas AlgR and streptococcal WalR. The receiver-to-DNA-binding mechanism is shared, but regulon, target promoters, regulatory sign and physiological process are set by the subfamily.
interpro/panther/PTHR48111/PTHR48111-rev.coherence_reason: The receiver-domain phosphorelay activity, cis-regulatory DNA binding and transcriptional regulation are shared family-wide and supported by many seeds in PANTHER's 49 subfamilies. Specific biology is not shared: KdpE (SF50) activates the kdpFABC potassium-pump operon, OmpR (SF4) is a dual activator and repressor of porin genes, ArcA (SF55) controls aerobic respiration genes, and so on. The direction of regulation and any process more specific than transcription regulation must therefore be assigned per subfamily.
